one-line thesis: Wakefit is scaling as India's leading omnichannel home and sleep solutions brand, leveraging strong brand equity and vertical integration to capture market share despite raw material inflation and competitive pressures, with strategic expansion into adjacent categories to boost customer lifetime value. The company's asset-light retail model and disciplined pricing are positioning it for sustained revenue growth, though near-term margins face pressure from input cost volatility.

segment / subsidiary detail: Mattresses: 61.4% of FY26 revenue, +17% YoY; Q4 growth +20%. Furniture: 29.3% revenue, +24% FY26, +14% Q4. Furnishings: 9.3% revenue. D2C + COCO channels contributed 74% of Q4 sales. MBOs: 1,948 locations. COCO stores: 139 as of Mar'26, 42 added, 8 closed (due to logistics, not demand).
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into adjacent categories: live plants, plant nutrients, soil conditioners, wall hangings, and home essentials via white-label/trade sourcing — no major capex, aimed at completing home ecosystem for Jumbo stores and increasing LTV. Jumbo store (100k+ sq ft) to launch in FY27.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin: 56% Q4, 55.8% FY26. Raw material inflation: 30-160% for key inputs (polyol, TDI, MDF); net COGS inflation ~10-30% post-stock utilization. Price increases: 7-8% in Mar and Apr '26 (cumulative 15%). EBITDA margin: 10.6% Q4, 12.2% FY26. Near-term margin pressure expected due to lagged price pass-through and higher A&P spend.
capex / expansion: FY26: INR29cr. FY27 guidance: INR120-140cr, primarily for retail — ~60-70% allocated to Jumbo store initial capex, remainder to 80+ new COCO stores. No manufacturing capacity expansion.
capital allocation: Net cash position: INR958cr as of Mar'26. No debt. Capital allocation prioritized toward retail expansion (COCO stores, Jumbo store), brand building (A&P), and product ecosystem expansion. No dividend or buyback mentioned. ESOPs to rise to INR12cr in FY27.
risks & watch-items: Raw material price volatility (crude-linked); competitive intensity from low-cost D2C and regional players; potential volume elasticity from 15% price hikes; margin compression from higher A&P spend; execution risk in scaling 80+ stores; regulatory approval pending for MOA amendment for new categories.
management quality / tone: Confident, strategic, and long-term oriented. Management emphasizes brand strength, customer retention, and LTV over short-term volume. Acknowledges near-term headwinds but frames them as industry-wide and temporary. Focus on market share protection, omnichannel dominance, and ecosystem expansion. Tone is disciplined, not aggressive on volume targets.
non-obvious takeaways: Wakefit's true moat is not just product quality but its flywheel: repeat purchases across mattress, furniture, and furnishings drive CRM-driven cross-selling. The 74% Q4 sales from owned channels (D2C + COCO) creates unparalleled customer data for retention. Adjacent categories (plants, fertilizers) are not revenue drivers but 'completeness' tools to lock in home-centric brand perception — a subtle but powerful differentiator.

hero.oneLiner: India's largest Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) home and furnishings brand, offering mattresses, furniture and home décor through a full-stack, vertically integrated business model and an omnichannel retail network spanning 700+ districts.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: India's largest Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) home and furnishings brand, offering mattresses, furniture and home décor through a full-stack, vertically integrated business model and an omnichannel retail network spanning 700+ districts.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Wakefit Innovations Limited is an engineering-led, vertically integrated D2C home and furnishings company operating across mattresses, furniture, and furnishings/décor for Indian households. It controls its value chain end-to-end from product conceptualisation, design, R&D and engineering through manufacturing, supply chain, logistics and direct customer engagement, selling via its website, online marketplaces, Company-Owned Company-Operated (COCO) stores and a Multi-Brand Outlet (MBO) network. The Company is the only organised player with complete control over upstream value-chain processes in both the mattress and furniture segments.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Mattresses: 61.4% of FY26 revenue, +17% YoY; Q4 growth +20%. Furniture: 29.3% revenue, +24% FY26, +14% Q4. Furnishings: 9.3% revenue. D2C + COCO channels contributed 74% of Q4 sales. MBOs: 1,948 locations. COCO stores: 139 as of Mar'26, 42 added, 8 closed (due to logistics, not demand).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Mattresses:** Memory Foam & ShapeSense, EcoLatex, Xpert Grid, Dual Comfort, Rollup & Foldable, Zense SleepTech
- **Furniture:** Beds, Sofas & Recliners, Wardrobes & Dressing Tables, Dining Sets & Chairs, Storage Solutions (TV units, cabinets, desks, shelves)
- **Furnishings & Décor:** Pillows & Cushions, Towels, Mats, Rugs & Carpets, Curtains & Bathrobes, Home Décor & Lighting, Kitchen & Tableware Accessories

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India (pan-India, 700+ districts)
- Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities (expansion focus)

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Full-stack vertically integrated: in-house design (CAD/CAM), engineering and manufacturing across five facilities, with cloud-linked machinery, SAP-ERP integration and cost-optimization initiatives (in-house lamination, EPEI, roll-pack and flat-pack technology). Distribution via one central mother warehouse (Hosur), 7 INHPs and 18 PODs as of Sep 30, 2025, supported by own installation teams. Direct customer engagement through website and COCO stores completes forward integration.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: FY27 revenue growth targeted via mattress strength and expanded furniture/furnishings reach; A&P spend to rise to 7-8% of sales; ESOP expenses expected at INR12cr (vs INR33cr in FY26); no material margin dilution expected in Q1FY27; 80+ net store additions planned.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion into adjacent categories: live plants, plant nutrients, soil conditioners, wall hangings, and home essentials via white-label/trade sourcing — no major capex, aimed at completing home ecosystem for Jumbo stores and increasing LTV. Jumbo store (100k+ sq ft) to launch in FY27.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's mattress market (valued at Rs 145-160 billion in CY2024) has grown at a 7-9% CAGR since CY2019 and is projected to grow at a 10-12% CAGR to Rs 270-300 billion by CY2030
- India's Home & Furnishings market (estimated at Rs 2.8-3.0 trillion in CY2024) is projected to grow to Rs 5.2-5.9 trillion by CY2030, at an 11-13% CAGR
- Furniture market segment (Rs 1,800-2,000 billion in CY2024) is projected to grow to Rs 3,200-3,900 billion by CY2030 at a 10-12% CAGR, and is nearly 10x larger than the mattress market, offering long-term growth headroom
- Furnishings and décor segment (Rs 790-860 billion in CY2024) is projected to grow at a 12-14% CAGR to Rs 1,630-1,810 billion by CY2030
- Growth in the smart mattress / sleep-tech segment (memory foam, hybrid constructions, sleep-tracking) is positioning the mattress as an active wellness tool for consumers prioritising health optimisation
- Rising disposable incomes, urbanisation (urban population projected to exceed 40% of India's population by 2030), growing middle-class consumer base and increasing nuclear family households are structurally driving demand for contemporary, space-efficient furnishing solutions
- Deepening penetration of organised retail and e-commerce, along with government-backed housing programs (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, Smart Cities Mission), is expanding market reach into Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities
- Mass segment commands 65% of the home furnishings market, structurally limiting headroom for premium pricing, particularly in Tier-2/Tier-3 cities
- Own-channel (website + COCO stores) contribution to total revenue rose to 67.2% in FY26 from 57.0% in FY25, supporting higher margins and stronger customer engagement
- Management notes robust residential real estate activity, rising household incomes and increased home-improvement spending are generating stronger consumer appetite for premium mattress offerings

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin: 56% Q4, 55.8% FY26. Raw material inflation: 30-160% for key inputs (polyol, TDI, MDF); net COGS inflation ~10-30% post-stock utilization. Price increases: 7-8% in Mar and Apr '26 (cumulative 15%). EBITDA margin: 10.6% Q4, 12.2% FY26. Near-term margin pressure expected due to lagged price pass-through and higher A&P spend.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Net cash position: INR958cr as of Mar'26. No debt. Capital allocation prioritized toward retail expansion (COCO stores, Jumbo store), brand building (A&P), and product ecosystem expansion. No dividend or buyback mentioned. ESOPs to rise to INR12cr in FY27.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Wakefit is deploying IPO fresh-issue proceeds toward accelerating its next phase of physical retail expansion: funding lease/sub-lease rentals and license fees for its existing COCO Regular Stores, capital expenditure for setting up 117 new COCO Regular Stores, and purchase of new equipment and machinery to enhance manufacturing capabilities. The Company is also planning to introduce large-format 'COCO Jumbo Stores' of 50,000 to 200,000 sq. ft. as regional flagship experience centres in key metropolitan markets, alongside continuing to expand its MBO partner network beyond its current base of approximately 1,948 stores. Separately, management points to planned investments in advanced manufacturing capacity to support furniture SKU expansion and unlock additional addressable opportunity, and to an 'Omnichannel Expansion' growth pillar targeting materially higher net COCO store additions per quarter from FY2027 onwards.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, strategic, and long-term oriented. Management emphasizes brand strength, customer retention, and LTV over short-term volume. Acknowledges near-term headwinds but frames them as industry-wide and temporary. Focus on market share protection, omnichannel dominance, and ecosystem expansion. Tone is disciplined, not aggressive on volume targets.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Only organised player with complete control over upstream value-chain processes in both the mattress and furniture segments, per Redseer
- Full-stack vertically integrated model spanning design, R&D, manufacturing, supply chain, logistics and direct customer engagement, enabling cost efficiency, quality control and faster innovation
- Largest and fastest-growing D2C home and furnishings brand in India, and the only D2C player with each of its three product categories generating over Rs 100 crore in annual revenue
- Strong brand equity underpinned by India's first industry-wide 100-day free trial and 100% refund policy for mattresses, a 4.3-4.4/5 product rating across major e-commerce platforms, and repeat customer revenue of 35.3% of revenue from operations
- Omnichannel distribution network combining company-owned digital platform, 139 COCO stores and 1,948 MBO stores across 536 cities, backed by a three-tier logistics network (1 Mother Warehouse, 9 Inventory Holding Points, 17 Points of Delivery)
- Geographically diversified, automated manufacturing footprint across five facilities in Haryana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu using lean production and the 'Every Part Every Interval' (EPEI) scheduling process

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Raw material price volatility (crude-linked); competitive intensity from low-cost D2C and regional players; potential volume elasticity from 15% price hikes; margin compression from higher A&P spend; execution risk in scaling 80+ stores; regulatory approval pending for MOA amendment for new categories.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Wakefit's true moat is not just product quality but its flywheel: repeat purchases across mattress, furniture, and furnishings drive CRM-driven cross-selling. The 74% Q4 sales from owned channels (D2C + COCO) creates unparalleled customer data for retention. Adjacent categories (plants, fertilizers) are not revenue drivers but 'completeness' tools to lock in home-centric brand perception — a subtle but powerful differentiator.

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Set up 117 new COCO - Regular Stores across India funded from Net Proceeds**
- **Open two COCO - Jumbo Stores (50,000-200,000 sq ft) in Bengaluru funded through internal accruals**
- **Purchase new equipment and machinery for Hosur (MF IV) furniture unit to expand engineered-wood line**
- **Grow revenue from own channels (website + COCO stores) and expand POD network for same-day delivery**
- **Enter interior designing services and expand MBO network**
- **Deploy Rs 1,084.04m of Net Proceeds towards marketing and advertisement over FY2027-FY2029**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Own-channel dominance: drive a higher share of revenue through the website and COCO stores versus external marketplaces and MBOs, to improve margins, customer engagement and operational control
- Deepen COCO store penetration into underserved Tier-2 and smaller-town markets through an asset-light store format while maintaining healthy unit economics
- Use the 1,948-strong MBO network to test and enter new geographies with limited upfront capital investment
- Continue innovation in sleep-tech (e.g. Zense AI-powered sleep ecosystem) and personalisation to enhance differentiation and margin …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Input-cost shock] "The quarter was marked by significant volatility in raw material prices following the Middle East situation, particularly across key mattress category inputs such as Polyol and TDI. The Middle East situation also impacted supply chain costs across the other categories."
- [Market size] Redseer CY24 TAM: mattresses US$1.7-1.9 Bn (~5% segment share of the CY2024 India home and furnishings market), furniture US$22-24 Bn (~66%), furnishing & decor US$9.5-10.4 Bn (~29%) — furniture is by far the largest pool relative to Wakefit's mattress-led revenue mix.
- [Deferred tax] FY26 PAT is stated as being "after the impact of Deferred Tax Asset of INR 980.7 mn", recognised in Q4FY26 under IndAS 12 following "increase in gratuity liability arising out of past service cost and increase in leave liability on account for changes in Labour laws"; the deck flags the subsequent movement as "non-cash, accounting-driven" with no impact on cash tax outflow.
- [Ownership/board] Nominee directors from Peak XV Partners (Sakshi Vijay Chopra) and Elevation Capital / Light Ray Advisors (Mukul Arora) sit on the board; promoters (Ankit Garg, Chaitanya Ramalingegowda) are also part of the board.
- [Corporate status] The company is "formerly known as Wakefit Innovations Private Limited", listed on BSE (544642) and NSE (WAKEFIT).
